Author: R. Raghunandan Rao Bench: R Raghunandan Rao APHC010105232008  IN THE HIGH COURT OF ANDHRA PRADESH  AT AMARAVATI [3525]
 (Special Original Jurisdiction)
 TUESDAY, THE FOURTH DAY OF MARCH  TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY FIVE  PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE R RAGHUNANDAN RAO  AND  THE HONOURABLE DR JUSTICE K MANMADHA RAO  Review I.A.No.1 of 2021  IN  CIVIL MISCELLANEOUS APPEAL Nos.987, 990 & 1014 of 2008 Between:
Kurra Venkateswara Rao, Kanchikacherla (m), Krishna Dist ...APPELLANT  AND Competent Authority La And Managerii Vijaywadakrishna ...RESPONDENT Dist Counsel for the Appellant:

sentences.text:
The Court made the following Common Order:
Heard Sri P. Prabhakar Rao, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri S.S. Varma,
learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.
2. The land of the petitioners, in Kanchikacharla Village, was acquired for the purposes of widening of National Highway-9.
The acquisition officer had conducted an enquiry regarding valuation of the land and awarded certain amounts as compensation.

Being aggrieved by the compensation fixed by the acquisition officer, under the provisions of the National Highway Act, 1956 [for short "the N.H Act"], a reference was made to the District Collector, under Section 3-G(5)(7) of the N.H Act for enhancement of compensation.
The Collector, acting as an Arbitrator, under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 [for short "the Arbitration Act, 1996"], had rejected the said application for enhancement.

Aggrieved by the said order of rejection, the petitioners herein had moved the District Court, which also rejected the application filed under Section 34 of the Dodda Rama Mohana Rao vs The National High Way Authority Of India on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48975384/
1 Arbitration Act, 1996.

entities.text: Dodda Rama Mohana Rao vs The National High Way Authority Of India on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the said Order of rejection by the District Court, the petitioners moved C.M.A.Nos.987, 990 & 1014 of 2008 under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act, 1996.

3. A Division Bench of this Court had passed a Common Order, in these Miscellaneous Applications,
on 01.05.2020.
The Division Bench after considering various submissions made by both sides was pleased to direct enhancement of compensation and fixed the market value of Rs.61/- per square meter.
4. Subsequent to the passing of this Order, the NHIA had recalculated the compensation payable at the market rate of Rs.61 per square meter and paid the said compensation.
5. Subsequent to this payment, the present set of review applications has been filed.

It is contended that the National Highway Authorities, while recalculating the compensation had not taken into account any payment of interest, on account of the delay in payment on the ground that the said Order had not contained any direction for payment of interest.

6. The petitioners have approached this Court contending that the omission of the Court in not directing payment of statutory benefits under the Act, including interest for delayed payment, is an error apparent on the face of the record as the said benefits are automatic and the only question as far as the interest is concerned, is the rate of interest that may be fixed by the Arbitrator.
7. The acquisition in the present case, was conducted during the existence of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [for short "the Act, 1894"].
Section 3(J) of the N.H. Act had specifically excluded the provisions of the Act, 1894 from being applicable to any acquisition conducted under the provisions of the N.H. Act.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sunita Mehra Vs. Union of India1 had taken the view that the same would not be permissible and that interest would have to be paid,
in terms of the Act, 1894.

entities.text: Sunita Mehra Vs. Union of India1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Union of India & anr Vs. Tarsem Singh &
Ors2

entities.text:
Union of India & anr Vs. Tarsem Singh &
Ors2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: had taken the view that Section 3(J), which excluded the applicability of the Act, 1894, to the provisions of the N.H. Act was unconstitutional.

The relevant paragraph No.52 of the said Judgment is extracted as here under:-
"There is no doubt that the learned Solicitor General, in the aforesaid two orders, has conceded the issue raised in these cases.

This assumes importance in view of the plea of Shri Divan that the impugned judgments (2019) 17 SCC 672 : 2016 SCC Online SC 1128 (2019) 9 SCC 304 should be set aside on the ground that when the arbitral awards did not provide for solatium or interest, no Section 34 petition having been filed by the landowners on this score, the Division Bench judgments that are impugned before us ought not to have allowed solatium and/or interest.

Ordinarily, we would have acceded to this plea, but given the fact that the Government itself is of the view that solatium and interest should be granted even in cases that arise between 1997 and 2015, in the interest of justice we decline to interfere with such orders, given our discretionary jurisdiction Dodda Rama Mohana Rao vs The National High Way Authority Of India on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48975384/
2 under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Dodda Rama Mohana Rao vs The National High Way Authority Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We therefore declare that the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in Section 23(1-A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of section 28 proviso will apply to acquisitions made under the National Highways Act.
Consequently, the provision of Section 3-J is, to this extent, violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and, therefore, declared to be unconstitutional.

Accordingly, Appeal @ SLP (C)
No. 9599/2019 is dismissed."
9. In the circumstances, the petitioners would be entitled for interest, to the extent of the delay, in payment of compensation to the petitioners.

Section 3-H(5) of N.H. Act stipulates that the affected person, would be entitled to interest, as may be fixed by the Arbitrator, subject to maximum of 9%
per annum, on the amount which has been enhanced.

10. In that view of the matter, the petitioners would be entitled to interest, from the date of the possession of the land being taken till the date of payment of enhanced compensation at a rate that was to be fixed by the Arbitrator, subject to a maximum of 9% per annum.
11.

In view of the fact that there was a huge delay in the payment of enhanced compensation, it would be appropriate to allow these Review Applications with a direction to the National Highway Authorities to pay interest at the rate of 9%, per annum, on the enhanced amounts from the date of taking of possession of the land of the petitioners, till the date of payment of enhanced compensation.
12. Accordingly, these Review Applications are allowed.
